In [[mathematics]], a '''double vector bundle''' is the combination of two compatible [[vector bundle]] structures, which contains in particular the tangent <math>TE</math> of a vector bundle <math>E</math> and the [[double tangent bundle]] <math>T^2M</math>.

==Definition and first consequences==
A '''double vector bundle''' consists of <math>(E, E^H, E^V, B)</math>, where 
# the ''side bundles'' <math>E^H</math> and <math>E^V</math> are vector bundles over the base <math>B</math>,
# <math>E</math> is a vector bundle on both side bundles <math>E^H</math> and <math>E^V</math>,
# the projection, the addition, the [[scalar multiplication]] and the zero map on ''E'' for both vector bundle structures are morphisms.

==Double vector bundle morphism==

A '''double vector bundle morphism''' <math>(f_E, f_H, f_V, f_B)</math> consists of maps <math>f_E : E \mapsto E'</math>,  <math>f_H : E^H \mapsto E^H{}'</math>,  <math>f_V : E^V \mapsto E^V{}'</math> and  <math>f_B : B \mapsto B'</math> such that <math>(f_E, f_V)</math> is a bundle morphism from <math>(E, E^V)</math> to <math>(E', E^V{}')</math>, <math>(f_E, f_H)</math> is a bundle morphism from <math>(E, E^H)</math> to <math>(E', E^H{}')</math>, <math>(f_V, f_B)</math> is a bundle morphism from <math>(E^V, B)</math> to <math>(E^V{}', B')</math> and <math>(f_H, f_B)</math> is a bundle morphism from <math>(E^H, B)</math> to <math>(E^H{}', B')</math>.

The '''flip'' of the double vector bundle <math>(E, E^H, E^V, B)</math> is the double vector bundle <math>(E, E^V, E^H, B)</math>.

==Examples==

If <math>(E, M)</math> is a vector bundle over a differentiable manifold <math>M</math> then <math>(TE, E, TM, M)</math> is a double vector bundle when considering its [[secondary vector bundle structure]].

If <math>M</math> is a [[differentiable manifold]], then its [[double tangent bundle]] <math>(TTM, TM, TM, M)</math> is a double vector bundle.
